fichas.title: Private Building Law: Project Legal Relationships
fichas.summary: Overview of the principal legal relationships in a building project. The client engages a contractor under a works contract, potentially specified as a building contract under VOB, and engages a designer under an architectural service contract governed by BGB and HOAI. The diagram also indicates authority to act through a power of attorney for the client. The text distinguishes a works contract, which aims at a contractually determined result such as construction of a building, from a service contract, whose subject is work as such.
uses: Explain contractual relationships among the client, contractor, and designer
Clarify the distinction between works contracts and service contracts

fichas.title: HOAI Work Phases and Fee Shares
fichas.summary: The page lists nine HOAI work phases and their respective percentages of the total fee. Phases 1–4 are grouped under design and phases 5–9 under construction. The accompanying text says fees depend on the fee zone, chargeable costs, and the work phases undertaken, and distinguishes basic services from separately ordered special services. It also describes a proposed revision of HOAI, including restriction to smaller projects, removal of work phases 6–9 and consulting services, and fees based on building costs agreed in advance.
uses: Organize architectural and engineering services by work phase
Relate completed work phases to fee shares

fichas.title: Comparison of BGB Works Contract Law and VOB/B
fichas.summary: A comparison table maps provisions of the German Civil Code (BGB) works contract law to corresponding VOB/B provisions. Topics include payment, defects and defect claims, supplementary performance, self-remedy, acceptance, risk, termination, and contractor or employer responsibilities. The text explains that VOB is freely agreed contract law rather than legislation, and outlines its three parts: Part A concerns tender documents and contract award procedures; Part B contains general conditions for construction contracts; Part C contains trade-specific general technical contract conditions, organized into five numbered subjects.
uses: Compare BGB works-contract provisions with corresponding VOB/B provisions
Describe the organization and scope of VOB parts A, B, and C
